description: Pre-built SQL queries for InHouse Print business intelligence - 50+ optimized queries for sales, customers, production, stock, and historical analysis

tools.name: get_available_queries
tools.description: List all available pre-built SQL queries from QueryLibrary. Use this FIRST to discover what business intelligence queries are available. Returns 50+ queries organized by category: Sales & Revenue (monthly trends, product breakdowns), Customer Analytics (top customers, retention), Production Planning (daily schedules, capacity), Stock Management (inventory levels, reorder alerts), Historical Quote Analysis (past quotes for parameter extraction). Each query includes description, parameters, visualization type, and best use cases.

category.description: Filter queries by category (optional). Use 'all' to see all 50+ queries, or specify a category to narrow results. Default: 'all'

returns.description: Success status, category filter applied, query count, and list of queries with name, description, parameters, category, visualization type, and best_for guidance

examples.description: Get all sales and revenue queries
examples.expected_result: Returns ~4 queries: sales_trend_by_month, monthly_revenue_trend, revenue_by_product_type, etc.
Returns customer-related queries: top_customers_detailed, customer_retention, etc.

tools.name: execute_query_library
tools.description: Execute a pre-built SQL query from QueryLibrary. ALWAYS call get_available_queries() FIRST to see available queries and their required parameters. Pre-built queries are optimized, tested, and include visualization metadata. Common queries: 'sales_trend_by_month' (sales over time), 'top_customers_detailed' (best customers), 'daily_production_plan' (jobs to produce), 'stock_inventory_master' (inventory levels), 'historical_business_card_quotes' (past business card orders for analysis). Each query accepts different parameters - check get_available_queries() for details.

query_name.description: Name of the query to execute (from get_available_queries). Examples: 'sales_trend_by_month', 'top_customers_detailed', 'daily_production_plan', 'stock_inventory_master', 'historical_flyer_quotes'. Must be exact match.

parameters.description: Query-specific parameters (optional, varies by query). Common parameters: {'months': 6} for time-based queries, {'top_n': 10} for top/bottom queries, {'days_ahead': 1} for production planning, {'customer_id': 123} for customer-specific queries. Each query has different parameters - use get_available_queries() to see required/optional parameters for each query.

returns.description: Query result with success status, query_name executed, parameters_used (includes defaults), data array (list of row dicts), and metadata (description, category, visualization type, row_count, best_for guidance). On error: success=False, error message, query_name, parameters attempted.

examples.description: Get sales trend for last 6 months
examples.expected_result: Returns monthly sales data with TotalRevenue, OrderCount, AvgOrderValue for each month. Includes visualization: 'line_chart'
Returns top 10 customers with CustomerName, TotalRevenue, OrderCount, AvgOrderValue. Includes visualization: 'bar_chart'
Returns jobs to produce tomorrow with TicketID, JobName, DueDate, EstimatedHours. Includes visualization: 'table'
Returns current stock levels with StockID, StockName, CurrentLevel, ReorderPoint, Status. Includes visualization: 'table'

examples.description: Find historical business card quotes for analysis
examples.expected_result: Returns past business card quotes with quantity, stock_type, sides, finish, price. Useful for extracting common parameters. Includes visualization: 'table'
